title: Give an Order a Clear Address
description: A shop is designing its order API. A client creates an order and needs its canonical address for later reads. Which contract communicates that clearly?

options.text: GET /createOrder returns 200 with the new order.
options.explanation: GET should not create resources. Creation belongs on a write method, so safe reads and intermediaries do not accidentally place orders.

options.text: POST /orders returns 201 and a Location header.
options.explanation: The collection is a resource, POST creates an order, and 201 plus Location tells the client where to read the new resource.

options.text: POST /orders returns 204 with no resource address.
options.explanation: 204 can indicate success without a body, but it does not communicate creation and the requested canonical address as clearly as 201 with Location.

options.text: GET /orders returns 200 with an error field when creation fails.
options.explanation: GET is for reading, and disguising an error as 200 breaks client recovery and monitoring.
